labels.content: 100% قطن / 100% COTTON · size 'S (54–56 cm)' / 'M (56–58 cm)' / 'L (58–60 cm)' · ISO 3758 symbols: wash 30 °C, no bleach, tumble dry low, iron low (max 110 °C), no dry-clean, plus Arabic care text (ES 1405) e.g. 'غسيل عادي 30° – لا يُبيّض – تجفيف بحرارة منخفضة – كي بحرارة منخفضة' and 'اغسل مع الألوان الداكنة أول مرتين' (wash with darks first 2 washes) · صنع في مصر / Made in Egypt · manufacturer or brand name and address (Arabic) · style number, CW code, batch/PO · brand contact.
labels.notes: Printed satin or recycled-poly loop, ≈ 3 × 6 cm folded. Egyptian domestic market: Arabic fibre content, care, origin and manufacturer are obligatory (ES 7266-3/2023, ES 7266-4, ES 1405); labels sewn in at the factory – stickers not accepted. Include the dark-first wash note because the black shell is stitched to the khaki shell (bleed risk).

labels.placement: Not separate – size is printed on the care label and on the polybag sticker / hangtag.
labels.content: S / M / L with cm range.
labels.notes: Avoids an extra visible label on a reversible hat. Optional: size letter also woven on the back of the brand label.

labels.placement: Attached with a cotton string + plastic lock (or safety pin) through the brand woven label loop. Hat folded with the designated OUTER face out.
labels.content: Brand, style name/number, 'Reversible / قابلة للعكس', colorway code and both swatch names: CW1 'Khaki / Black' – 'كاكي / أسود', CW2 'Black / Khaki' – 'أسود / كاكي', size with cm, barcode/SKU per colorway, price field, 100% cotton, Made in Egypt.
labels.notes: Second differentiator for the two colorways (with the polybag sticker). No tagging gun anywhere on the hat.

packaging: Fold: crown flat, brim folded under, designated outer face out (CW1 khaki, CW2 black); hangtag visible through the bag.
Polybag: clear LDPE 25 × 35 cm, 40 µm, self-seal flap, printed suffocation warning in Arabic and English, recycled-content mark; one hat per bag.
Polybag sticker (top right): brand, style no., colorway code CW1/CW2 with colour names, size S/M/L (cm range), EAN/SKU barcode (separate SKU per colorway and size), 'Made in Egypt / صنع في مصر'.
Inner pack: 12 pcs solid size / solid colorway in a polybag bundle (ratio packs only if the brand instructs).
Export/master carton: 24 pcs (2 inners), 5-ply corrugated ≈ 36 × 36 × 30 cm, gross ≈ 3.5 kg (hat ≈ 100 g + bag/tag ≈ 12 g); max 12 kg per carton if the brand asks for 48 pcs.
Carton marks (2 opposite sides): brand, style, colorway, size, quantity, carton n of N, gross/net weight, dimensions, 'Made in Egypt', handling symbols; packing list inside carton 1.
Packing list / shipping mark must state colorway by code AND colour names because the hats in CW1 and CW2 cartons are physically identical – only label side and folding differ.
No metal tags, no pins in the fabric, no silica gel in contact with the hat.
qc: Sampling: ISO 2859-1, General Inspection Level II, single sampling, normal; AQL 2.5 major / 4.0 minor. Example lot 281–500 pcs: code H, n = 50, major Ac 3 / Re 4, minor Ac 5 / Re 6; lot 151–280: code G, n = 32, major Ac 2/Re 3, minor Ac 3/Re 4; lot 501–1,200: code J, n = 80, major Ac 5/Re 6, minor Ac 7/Re 8. Critical (needle fragment, wrong label content/origin, wrong colorway label side): Ac 0.

Inspect EVERY sampled hat on BOTH faces (turn it) – a defect on either face counts. Reversible-specific majors: bobbin colour showing through on either face; brim edge seam rolled >2 mm to one face; band/brim seams of the two shells misaligned >0.5 cm; brims separating (ditch row missed); label stitching visible on the outer face; press shine on black; gap not fully closed by topstitch; hat pair mismatched sizes.

Measurement audit: first 20 hats per size 100% measured (A on both faces, B, C, D, G); then 10 pcs per size per lot. Tolerances per POM table; A out of ±1.0 cm or D out of ±0.5 cm = major. Record on the graded spec sheet, sign off before packing.

Colorway audit: for each lot, verify by sample that CW1 hats carry both labels on the BLACK shell and are packed khaki-out, CW2 on the KHAKI shell packed black-out; sticker/hangtag CW code matches label side. Wrong label side = critical (it is the only thing that makes the SKUs different).

Fabric tests per colour lot before cutting: gsm 280 ±5% (ISO 3801); dimensional change ≤3% warp/weft after 3 × 40 °C wash (ISO 6330 / ISO 5077); colourfastness to washing ISO 105-C06 A1S ≥4 change, ≥3–4 staining on cotton; rubbing ISO 105-X12 dry ≥4 / wet ≥3 (black); cross-staining test: wash one finished sample hat 3× at 40 °C – khaki shell staining ≥4 grey scale.
Sewing thread / needle: needle change every shift or on any burr; 100% needle-count log; broken-needle procedure (Nm 80/90 fragments – metal-detect finished goods if the brand's channel requires it).

In-line checks: first-off approval of each operator (seam allowance 1.0 ±0.1 cm, SPI 10–11 seams / 8–9 topstitch, topstitch offset 0.6 ±0.1 cm), then 2-hourly roving audit of 5 pcs; brim topstitch parallelism checked at 4 points.
Finished hat weight audit: M ≈ 97 g ±8% (S 92 / L 102) – quick check that no ply or fusible was substituted.

Sample sequence before bulk: fit sample size M (decide brim option and label side), then size set S/M/L, then one PP sample per colorway (CW1 and CW2) sealed with the label side and fold direction shown, then TOP samples 2 per colorway per size from bulk.

Shade continuity: cut each hat's khaki and black shells from single shade groups; record roll numbers per bundle; shade check under D65 against approved lab dip (Pantone TCX) – delta E ≤1.0 within lot.
Pressing: press cloth mandatory on black; no shine, no seam imprint; crown round on head form; brim natural drop ≈ 30° both faces.

colour_refs.name: Khaki (shell colour 1 – outer for CW1, reverse for CW2; thread DTM; topstitch needle thread)
Jet Black (shell colour 2 – reverse for CW1, outer for CW2; thread DTM; topstitch bobbin thread)

assumptions: FROM BRIEF: 100% cotton twill ~280 gsm; reversible; two colorways khaki/black and black/khaki; sizes S/M/L; single-row brim topstitch; metric; first production run for a small Egyptian brand; 2 cm grade per size.

DERIVED (formulas stated in POM table): A = H_nom + 2; T = A − 2.5; D = T/π; E = B + C; F = A + 2π·C·cos30°; W = A/π + 2·C·cos30°; brim development radii R_i = (A/2π)/cos30°, sector 311.8°; band frustum r_top = T/2π, r_bottom = A/2π; consumption from net cut areas ÷ marker efficiency ÷ usable width.

INDUSTRY DEFAULTS (not from brief, adjust at fit sample): nominal heads 55/57/59 (ranges 54–56 / 56–58 / 58–60); 2 cm ease; band taper 2.5 cm; crown side height 9.0 cm at M with 0.5 cm/size grade; brim width 6.5 cm ungraded; brim drop 30°; 1.0 cm SA; topstitch 0.6 cm; turning gap 8 cm; label 1.5 cm below tip seam; 301 lockstitch, 10–11 / 8–9 SPI; Tex 30 seam / Tex 40 topstitch; needle Nm 80 / 90; 75% marker efficiency; 145 cm usable width; AQL 2.5/4.0 GII; polybag/carton spec; all SAM values.

Fabric width assumed 150 cm nominal / 145 cm usable, sanforized ≤3%. If the brand sources a local Egyptian mill at 145 cm nominal, consumption rises to ≈0.18 m per colour per hat; if fabric is not sanforized the factory pre-washes the lot (adds 1–2 days and ~3% length loss – buy 0.20 m).

Two-panel side band with side seams (not a single CB seam) and two-piece brim; plain round crown (no 6-panel); no eyelets, no chin cord, no sweatband, no lining, no adjuster – all confirmed absent per 'plain' brief.

Order quantity and size ratio not given; consumption uses S:M:L = 1:2:1 and the AQL example uses a 281–500 pcs lot. Both colorways assumed 50/50 – fabric need per colour is identical whatever the split because every hat uses one khaki and one black shell.

Labelling for Egyptian domestic sale (Arabic + English, ES 7266-3/2023 fibre/care/origin/manufacturer, ES 1405 care symbols) – no EU/US export label fields included; add RN / EU 1007/2011 fibre wording if exported.

Seam class reference for the bagged brim edge (ISO 4916 1.06.03, SSae) from the A&E seam-type matrix (https://www.amefird.com/wp-content/uploads/2009/10/Seam-Type.pdf); Pantone values from pantone.com (16-0726 TCX #A39264, 19-0303 TCX #2D2C2F); ISO 2859-1 GII code letters/Ac-Re from the standard tables (https://tetrainspection.com/aql-guide/).

Marker efficiency 75% is an assumption for curved brim pieces on a one-way twill; the factory's CAD marker for the actual size ratio overrides it – report actual efficiency and metres per hat back on the cutting report.
Thread consumption ≈ 3 × seam length for 301 on 2–4 plies of 280 gsm is a rule-of-thumb; the brim topstitch through 4 plies + ditch row are the biggest consumers of Tex 40.
notes: CW1 (khaki outer / black reverse) and CW2 (black outer / khaki reverse) are PHYSICALLY THE SAME HAT: same two shells, same seams, same khaki-needle/black-bobbin topstitch, same fabric consumption per colour, same SAM. Cut and sew all shells as one pool; the only branch is step 7/8 – which colour shell receives the brand label and care label (CW1 → black shell, CW2 → khaki shell) – plus the hangtag CW code, polybag sticker/SKU and the fold direction at packing. If the brand prefers one SKU, drop the CW split entirely and put labels on the black shell (or a double-sided brim-seam loop label) and pack 50/50 either way out.

Reversible = no wrong side anywhere: every seam allowance is trapped between the two shells; no overlock, no topstitch on internal seams (would show on one face only), band side seams pressed OPEN, labels stitched to a single shell before nesting so their stitching is hidden between shells. Any operation that stitches through both shells after turning (topstitch, ditch) must use khaki needle / black bobbin with khaki face up.

Geometry consistency: tip diameter is derived from the band top circumference (D = (A − 2.5)/π) so the tip circle closes without ease; its grade is 0.64 cm per size, not 2 cm. Brim outer circumference and width depend on the 30° brim drop – if the brand wants a flatter brim the pattern sector angle changes (flat brim = 360°, F = A + 40.8) and F/W must be regraded.

The inner shell sits inside the outer shell; at 0.5 mm fabric thickness the circumference difference is ≈3 mm – ignored (both shells cut from the same pattern). Measure A on both faces; a difference >0.5 cm indicates misaligned band/brim seams, not a pattern issue.

Colour risk is asymmetric: black bleeding onto khaki inside the same hat cannot be fixed after production – test the black lot for wash and wet-rub fastness and wash one finished sample before bulk cutting. The care label tells the consumer to wash with darks for the first two washes.

Marker/IE: twill allows 180° rotation of pieces (diagonal unchanged) but not flipping; interlock rotated brim halves to lift efficiency from ~75% toward 78–80%. One marker serves both colours – plan lays per colour with identical ply counts so shell counts match exactly (every hat needs one of each). A 3% shortfall in either colour stops the whole run.

Brim stiffness: base spec is the soft, packable brim (no interfacing, one topstitch row as briefed). If the fit sample flops, the cheapest fix is 3 concentric rows at 0.6/1.2/1.8 cm (+1.5 SAM) rather than fusible; decide at fit sample and freeze before the size set.

Cost drivers for a first small run: fabric ≈ 0.34 m per hat (0.17 × 2 colours) ≈ 94 g; labour 15.5 SAM; two label types + hangtag; minimum-run overheads on woven labels and lab dips (order labels for the full colorway split up front).
